title: Moss and the Rhyme Pot
checkpoint: Phase 1 (Introduction) — rhythm and rhyme. Read this one ALOUD to the children.
note_for_grown_ups: An Introduction-phase book — no decoding, you read it aloud. Leave a long pause before the last word of each rhyming pair and let the children supply it. If they miss it, say it together and read the page again.

pages.text: Moss found an old flower pot under the bench. He decided it was a rhyme pot.
pages.join_in: Clap the beat while you say it: rhyme — pot! rhyme — pot!
pages.illustration: Under the wooden garden bench, dim and cosy. Moss the berry-brown hedgehog nose-deep in a chipped terracotta pot, dry leaves all around his bedding. Dust motes in a slice of light coming under the bench.

pages.text: "Whatever you drop in," he said, "comes out with a friend. Watch. In goes a cat —"
pages.join_in: "— and out comes a … " (hat! bat! mat!)
pages.illustration: Moss dropping a small drawn picture-card of a cat into the pot with great ceremony. Fig the leaf-green striped caterpillar watches from the bench leg above, unconvinced, one eyebrow raised.

pages.text: In went a log. Out came a frog.
pages.join_in: Log — frog. Say them one after the other. Do they sound the same at the end?
pages.illustration: Split page: left, a mossy log tipping into the pot; right, a startled frog sitting on the pot rim mid-blink. Match the shapes of log and frog so the pairing is visual too.

pages.text: In went a spoon. Out came the moon. Fig said that could not possibly be right.
pages.join_in: Spoon — moon. Now say them in a big slow voice.
pages.illustration: A comically enormous pale moon squeezing up out of a small flower pot, filling the top half of the page, with a wooden spoon lying discarded below. Fig with all his little legs on his hips, exasperated. Moss delighted.

pages.text: In went Fig. Out came — a wig.
pages.join_in: Fig — wig! Say it, then giggle. You are allowed.
pages.illustration: Fig emerging from the pot wearing a ridiculous curly grey wig several sizes too big, stripes still showing underneath. Moss laughing so hard his spikes have gone flat. Silly and warm.

pages.text: So they sat in the dark under the bench, dropping in words, until the moon really did come out.
pages.join_in: Your turn. Say a word — can everybody find one that rhymes with it?
pages.illustration: Wide, quiet closing scene from outside the bench looking in. Two small silhouettes side by side, the pot between them, the real moon high above the garden. Deep blues with one warm spot of light on the pot.
